audit_findings.title: The anchor year keeps a disclosed non-recurring gain the filing itself quantifies
audit_findings.magnitude: $419m gain net of $51m legal expenses, less $116m incentive-comp and $82m discretionary-bonus offsets = $221m pre-tax; the filing states the net effect as $0.14 of diluted EPS, i.e. about $158m after tax on 1,128m diluted shares (~3.5% of the $4,569.4m anchor). At the base scenario each $100m of anchor OE is worth $1.26/share, so this is about $2.00 of the $62.91 base value and about $1.40 of the $44.04 buy_below.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters through the anchor. The FY2026 OE of $4,569.4m reconciles to net income $5,494m + D&A $1,247m - capex $1,957m - SBC $214m = $4,570m, so the anchor is the reported year with the settlement gain inside net income and nothing removed. Because 4c ruled the record untrendable, MIN(trend, latest) collapsed to latest and the one-off is capitalised in perpetuity at roughly 15x plus the fade and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The credit card interchange fees litigation settlement and related expenses resulted in a net benefit of $0.14 on diluted earnings per share in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated inclusion, not a possibility: the arithmetic identity above ties the anchor to reported net income to within $0.6m, and the company itself labels the item non-recurring in Note A. The judge named the $419m gain in the too-hard reason and then valued on the year containing it. The scale is real but modest - roughly 3.5% of the anchor and $2/share of value - and on its own it does not change the buy/no-buy answer at a $132.19 price against a $44.04 gate. It matters because it is a rule violation at the single most load-bearing input in a valuation that has no trend to fall back on, and because it points the same direction as the growth-rate flattery the judge already flagged.
audit_findings.action: Open the 4b extraction for FY2026 in the run folder and confirm whether the OE build starts from reported net income. If it does, re-run 4d with an anchor of roughly $4,411m (net of the $221m pre-tax item at the 24.7% effective rate) and record the revised base value/share and buy_below. If the pipeline's policy is deliberately to keep non-recurring items in a latest-actual anchor, that policy needs to be written into PIPELINE.md rather than left implicit.

audit_findings.title: A new recurring tariff regime post-dates the anchor year, while both the anchor and FY2027 carry tariff relief
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: TJX estimates approximately $490m of IEEPA tariffs paid in aggregate; $331m was refunded in Q2 FY2027 with $112m of incremental compensation accrued against it, a net $219m benefit ($0.14 diluted EPS) recognised in FY2027, not FY2026. The replacement global tariff rate is not quantified anywhere in the filings. The audit's 30-80bp merchandise-margin haircut on ~$60bn of sales ($180-480m pre-tax, $135-361m after tax, $1.71-4.55/share) is the auditor's own estimate, not a filed figure.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters through the anchor's cost of sales ratio and through the bear-case growth floor. The 69.0% cost-of-sales ratio that produced the FY2024-FY2026 step-up was earned under a tariff regime that has since been invalidated and replaced; a permanent gross-margin step-down would put forward OE below the anchor, which the 0% bear case structurally cannot express.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to the U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling, an executive order was issued imposing a new global tariff, in addition to any existing non-IEEPA tariffs.
audit_findings.explanation: The audit is right that the pipeline has no way to express a bear case below the anchor, and that is the substantive point. One factual correction to the record: the $331m of IEEPA refunds sits in Q2 FY2027, after the FY2026 anchor year, so it does not flatter the anchor - the judge's too-hard reason states otherwise. The anchor in fact bore IEEPA tariff cost that is now being refunded (understating), while the new global tariff is a cost the anchor never bore (overstating); the two run opposite ways and neither is quantifiable from the filings, which is why this is MIXED rather than directional. This is classified MONITOR because the new regime is not in any reported number yet - the executive order post-dates both the 10-K and the 10-Q's measurement period, the rate is undisclosed, and TJX has not recorded a receivable for further refunds.
audit_findings.action: Two separate items. (a) Confirm from the 4b extraction whether IEEPA tariff cost in FY2026 was treated as recurring or non-recurring, and correct the too-hard reason's attribution of the $331m refund to the anchor year. (b) Re-run 4d after the Q3 FY2027 10-Q, when the new global tariff rate and any further CBP refund phases are quantifiable, and consider whether the doctrine should permit a bear case below the anchor when a post-anchor regime change is documented in the filings.

audit_findings.title: $6,004m of cash added to the bridge gross, with the 10-Q liabilities block never parsed
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed at the bridge date (Aug 1, 2026): cash and cash equivalents $6,004m - the balance sheet shows no separate short-term investments line, so the figure appears to be cash only. Claims disclosed but not read: $229m uncertain tax positions and $835m long-term employee compensation (both as of Jan 31, 2026; other long-term liabilities were $1,168m at Aug 1, 2026), plus $22m accrued interest and penalties on a $286m gross unrecognised benefit. Against these, $595.3m of Executive Savings Plan rabbi-trust assets sit in Other assets and are not in the bridge. Gross claims are about $0.95/share; net of the trust assets the exposure is plausibly $0.20-0.40/share against a $62.91 base and $5.38/share of cash.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters through the bridge only, dollar for dollar: equity value = operating PV + cash, with debt deliberately not deducted under the equity-level OE convention. Any claim netted against cash reduces value per share one-for-one at 1/1,115.93m per dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: See Note M—Accrued Expenses and Other Liabilities, Current and Long-Term of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for long-term liabilities for which it is not reasonably possible for us to predict when they may be paid, which includes $835 million for employee compensation and benefits and $229 million for uncertain tax positions.
audit_findings.explanation: The deterministic audit returned a WARN that the liabilities block of the latest 10-Q could not be parsed, so the asset side was taken while the claims against it were never read - the record genuinely cannot establish materiality here, which is what makes this uncertain rather than material or immaterial. The likely size is small: the uncertain tax reserve is about a fifth of a dollar per share, and the $835m employee compensation liability is substantially matched by $595m of trust assets the bridge also ignores, so the two omissions partly cancel. The repatriation point is weaker than stated - the 10-Q says foreign cash is $1.6bn with only about $730m indefinitely reinvested working capital, and that repatriation is not expected to incur additional tax expense beyond withholding already provided for.
audit_findings.action: Parse the Aug 1, 2026 10-Q liability block by hand and record three things: whether $6,004m is cash only or cash plus short-term investments; whether the rabbi-trust assets should be added to the bridge alongside the employee compensation liability being deducted; and whether the $229m uncertain tax reserve nets against cash under house convention. Then re-run 4d only if the net exceeds a threshold worth recording, and write the convention into PIPELINE.md either way so the next name does not re-litigate it.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor reconciles to net income + D&A − capex − SBC, i.e. share-based compensation charged twice
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed SBC: $214m in FY2026, $183m in FY2025, $160m in FY2024. Computed: net income $5,494m + D&A $1,247m - capex $1,957m = $4,784m; less $214m = $4,570m against the $4,569.4m anchor, a $0.6m residual on a $4.6bn figure. $214m is 4.7% of the anchor and about $2.70 of the $62.91 base value per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters through the numerator of every judged year. SBC is already an expense inside net income; subtracting it again after a net-income start charges the same cost twice, while the denominator separately carries the full 1,115.93m diluted count. Because SBC grew from $160m to $214m over three years, the effect also depresses the later years of the series more than the earlier ones.
audit_findings.evidence: Total compensation cost related to share-based compensation was $ 214 million, $ 183 million and $ 160 million in fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The reconciliation is close to conclusive - a $0.6m residual across four filed line items is not coincidence - but it is inference from an identity rather than a reading of the 4b formula, so I am calling it a strong finding that still needs the formula confirmed. If the build starts from cash from operations instead, where SBC is added back before being subtracted, there is no double charge and the identity above is an accident of offsetting working-capital items. The direction is conservative, which is why it has not shown up as a problem, but it is a coherence defect in every year of the series and it interacts with the bear case: the FY2017-FY2023 flat stretch that justifies 0% growth is depressed by a rising SBC charge, which makes a genuinely flat business look slightly worse than flat. Roughly offsets finding 1 in size and direction.
audit_findings.action: Read the 4b extraction formula in the run folder and determine the starting line. If it starts from net income and subtracts SBC, re-run 4b through 4d for all ten years - not just the anchor - and check whether the corrected FY2017-FY2023 series still supports the 0% bear rate and the untrendable ruling. If it starts from cash from operations, record the reconciliation coincidence in PIPELINE.md so the next audit does not raise it again.

audit_findings.title: $566m of equity-method stakes are in neither the earnings nor the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed carrying values at the bridge date (Aug 1, 2026): MOS $223m (49% stake) plus BFL $334m (35% stake) = $557m; at FY2026 year-end $218m + $348m = $566m. Purchased for $551m in FY2025. $557m is $0.50 per share against a $62.91 base value, 0.8%; against the $88.15 gap between the $132.19 price and the $44.04 buy_below it is 0.6% of the distance.
audit_findings.mechanism: Would enter through the bridge as stakes_net, which currently carries 0.0. It cannot enter through OE because the company states the earnings from both investments are immaterial and are reported on a one-quarter lag, so the stakes contribute essentially nothing to the earnings series either.
audit_findings.evidence: The earnings from these investments did not have a material impact on the Company’s results for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The audit is factually right that the assets are captured nowhere and that the step-3 skip condition misfired - Note A discloses two equity-method investments with real carrying value. But the omission understates value by half a dollar per share on a sixty-three dollar base, and it points the safe way. That is a process defect worth fixing, not a valuation defect worth re-running for. Treat the missing $0.50 as stated conservatism until the step-3 rule is corrected, at which point it comes back on the next refresh anyway.
audit_findings.action: Fix the step-3 skip condition so 'nothing to value' tests for equity-method investments in Note A rather than for consolidated subsidiaries alone, and record the rule change in PIPELINE.md. Add $557m to stakes_net on the next scheduled refresh rather than triggering a re-run now; if left out, state the exclusion explicitly on the board so the conservatism is visible.

audit_findings.title: Multiemployer withdrawal liability is a claim ahead of equity that OE does not carry
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified. Filed: $27m of annual contributions in each of FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 to four plans; the Legacy Plan of the National Retirement Fund and the Legacy Plan of the UNITE HERE Retirement Fund are both in critical zone status with rehabilitation plans adopted, and the UNITE HERE Legacy plan has received Special Financial Assistance under ARPA. TJX's allocable share of underfunding is not disclosed in the 10-K. For scale, the single-employer position is a net asset: the funded plan is $189m overfunded against a $119m unfunded supplemental plan.
audit_findings.mechanism: Would enter through the bridge as an off-balance-sheet claim ahead of common equity, deducted from cash. It cannot enter through OE, which carries only the $27m of recurring annual contributions - those are correctly inside the earnings series already.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, based on information available to TJX, the Pension Protection Act Zone status for each of the Legacy Plan of the National Retirement Fund and the Legacy Plan of the UNITE HERE Retirement Fund is critical, rehabilitation plans have been adopted by these plans, and the Legacy Plan of the UNITE HERE Retirement Fund has received Special Financial Assistance under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a genuine off-balance-sheet claim the pipeline's bridge rules do not anticipate, and the audit is right to name it. It is classified MONITOR rather than uncertain because the liability is contingent on an event that has not occurred and is not planned - withdrawal is triggered by closing or reorganising the unionised US and Canadian distribution network, and TJX is expanding that network, not shrinking it. Nothing in the current numbers is wrong. The Special Financial Assistance received by the UNITE HERE Legacy plan cuts in the company's favour, since ARPA money reduces the underfunding an employer's allocable share is measured against. Against a $70.2bn base equity value, even a large allocable share would need to be in the billions to matter.
audit_findings.action: On the next refresh, pull the most recent Form 5500 Schedule MB for both Legacy plans and record the estimated withdrawal liability if disclosed. If it is material relative to the bridge, note it as a stated exclusion on the board rather than deducting an estimate. Re-check whenever TJX announces a distribution-centre closure, consolidation or divestiture in the US or Canada - that is the event that converts this from contingent to real.
